probability_semantics: Estimate F1-F10 suitability independently for the operator, cases, hardware and compiler. Methods combine; probabilities need not sum to one. Scores are exploration priors, not measured performance guarantees. Variants specify concrete options.
caveats: Source-based catalog; paper claims are unverified and rankings are not universal.
Verify hardware, resources and Triton Ascend/CANN APIs; capabilities do not transfer automatically across architectures.
L2 cache is not DSM. Capacity does not guarantee residency or eliminate HBM traffic. F6 needs an expressible, verified communication mechanism.
Separate kernels, streams and compiler scheduling still require valid ordering, visibility, synchronization and buffer lifetimes.
Archived measurements from another framework do not prove Triton performance. Verify correctness and measure all required work under one protocol.
F5 dispatches concrete plans such as F1/F2; it is not a low-level fusion primitive. F7 is a search policy. F8/F9 can overlap with F2.
Assess live tiles and lifetimes, not only tensor size. Fewer kernels/materializations do not guarantee speed.
Test fresh input, weight and bias across calls. Reuse allocations without stale contents; cover required cases/dtypes.
Compatibility is conditional; methods may suit only legal subgraphs or case subsets.

Target framework is Triton with the triton-ascend NPU backend. GPU-only APIs, warp/SM assumptions and paper prototypes require independent backend verification. Unsupported methods remain candidates for scoring but must not be presented as implementable.
Use real strides, correct boundary masks and accumulator precision in each Triton plan. Program instances do not imply a global barrier or addressable shared tiles across programs.

methods.name: Kernel Fission / Partial Fusion
methods.summary: Split a compound operator into independently tuned kernels, optionally fusing within each partition.
graph_conditions: Stages prefer different schedules, layouts or execution resources.
Intermediate materialization preserves the operator contract.
case_features: Full fusion has costly synchronization or resource pressure.
Compute and epilogue need different tiling or parallelism.
hardware_requirements: Supported kernels and dependency ordering for every partition.
Device-memory capacity for intermediate workspaces.
methods.execution_organization: Multiple dependent kernels, each with its own pipeline and a valid completion/dependency mechanism.
methods.dataflow: Input -> producer -> device-memory workspace -> consumer -> output; cache hits do not guarantee an HBM-free boundary.
benefits: Reduce simultaneous on-chip state and intra-kernel coordination.
risks: Extra launches and intermediate traffic.
Workspace and boundary layout-conversion costs.

variants.name: Compute / epilogue split
variants.description: Materialize compute results; run activation, conversion or layout work in a separately tuned kernel.

variants.name: Partially fused partitions
variants.description: Fuse compatible work inside partitions while retaining costly resource or layout boundaries.

variants.name: Primitive decomposition and orchestration
variants.description: Decompose into tensor primitives and compare legal groupings; use F7 for explicit partition search.

implementation_checks: Benchmark every partition and mandatory preprocessing.
Validate intermediate dtype, layout, padding, lifetime and ordering.
Compare complete-scope launch, memory and conversion costs.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.

methods.name: Vertical Fusion
methods.name_zh: 垂直融合／单 kernel 全融合
methods.summary: Fuse a producer-consumer chain and retain legal intermediate tiles on chip within one kernel.
graph_conditions: A consumer depends on a producer.
Tiling permits consumption of ready intermediate data.
case_features: Compute plus bias, activation, casting or compatible layout work.
Traffic/launch savings are material and live tiles fit resources.
hardware_requirements: Backend supports all operations in one kernel.
Adequate registers/local memory and supported transfers/synchronization.
methods.execution_organization: One kernel coordinates producer and consumer tiles, possibly across compute and vector sections.
methods.dataflow: Producer tile -> registers/local memory -> consumer tile -> output, removing selected intermediate materialization.
risks: Resource pressure, lower parallelism or spills.
Transfer/synchronization cost and pipeline imbalance.

variants.name: Compute with fused epilogue
variants.description: Apply bias, activation and conversion to completed compute tiles before final output stores.

variants.name: Compatible loop-chain fusion
variants.description: Combine compatible dependent loops while preserving reduction boundaries.

variants.name: Tiled producer-consumer pipeline
variants.description: Overlap successive tiles with supported buffering and synchronization; tune live resource use.

implementation_checks: Count all live tiles, buffers and compiler storage.
Verify transfer layout, synchronization and precision.
Inspect spills, stalls and occupancy; one kernel is not automatically optimal.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.

methods.name: Horizontal Fusion
methods.summary: Run independent operations in a shared kernel to improve utilization and amortize launches.
graph_conditions: Branches are independent during fused execution.
Input/output and side-effect ordering remain valid.
case_features: Small independent operations underutilize the device.
Independent compute/memory workloads may complement each other.
hardware_requirements: Backend supports independent work regions and legal resource partitioning.
Enough resources for concurrent regions.
methods.execution_organization: Partition work items or execution resources among independent regions within one kernel.
methods.dataflow: Separate inputs -> independent regions -> separate outputs; intermediate elimination is not the primary mechanism.
benefits: Improve utilization of small independent work.
Amortize launches and overlap complementary resource use.
risks: Contention, imbalance and combined resource pressure.
Mistaking dependent auxiliary work for independent work.

variants.name: Complementary independent regions
variants.description: Combine independent compute-heavy and memory-heavy regions with supported resource partitioning.

variants.name: Independent small branches
variants.description: Group independent small operations to increase work per launch.

implementation_checks: Prove independence from the graph.
Verify resource partition, output ownership and race freedom.
Measure interference and load balance against separate kernels.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.

methods.name: Input / Output Fusion
methods.summary: Share inputs or a producer among branches while preserving every required output.
graph_conditions: Branches share inputs or consume the same producer.
Traversal and output ownership can be coordinated.
case_features: Duplicate reads or producer computation matter.
Multi-output regions, such as several activations of one result.
hardware_requirements: Backend supports the required regions and outputs.
Enough local storage for shared data and branch state.
methods.execution_organization: Coordinate shared traversal or producer tiles across consumers; retain necessary unfused branches.
methods.dataflow: Shared input/producer tile -> locally reused data -> multiple branches -> all required outputs.
risks: Longer shared-data lifetimes and more branch state.
Incompatible layouts/reductions add coordination costs.

variants.name: Shared-input branches
variants.description: Read shared tiles once and apply multiple compatible branches.

variants.name: Producer with multiple consumers
variants.description: Retain producer tiles for multiple consumers instead of separately materializing and rereading them.

variants.name: Required multi-output execution
variants.description: Share work while emitting every observable output, including producer results still needed externally.

implementation_checks: Map all consumers and externally visible outputs.
Check branch-specific dtype, layout and reduction needs.
Measure sharing gains against storage and scheduling costs.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.
source_sections: F4: Input / Output Fusion（输入输出融合）

methods.name: Hybrid Routing
methods.name_zh: 混合路由／按 shape 分发
methods.summary: Route metadata-defined case groups to validated concrete fusion or tiling variants.
graph_conditions: Several implementations satisfy one complete contract.
A legal dispatcher can inspect relevant metadata.
case_features: Shape, dtype, layout or parameters change the best plan.
A small case group needs specialized tiling or fusion.
hardware_requirements: Supported dispatch and compilable variants.
Complete permitted-case coverage or a valid fallback.
methods.execution_organization: Dispatch to a concrete implementation such as F1/F2; routing itself is not a low-level fusion primitive.
methods.dataflow: Permitted metadata -> selected variant -> complete variant execution -> contractual outputs.
risks: Variant growth, compilation cost and fragile boundaries.
Noise overfitting, benchmark-identity routing or stale cached data.

variants.name: Fusion-boundary routing
variants.description: Select plans such as F1/F2 using measured metadata-defined case groups.

variants.name: Schedule and tile routing
variants.description: Keep the fusion family while selecting tiles, layouts or buffers for different case groups.

variants.name: Specializations with fallback
variants.description: Use justified specializations plus a correct fallback; record predicates and affected cases.

implementation_checks: Document metadata predicates; test routes and boundaries.
Test fresh tensor values across calls; reuse allocations, not stale contents.
Measure dispatch and mandatory preprocessing consistently.
Validate precision on every selected path.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.

methods.name: Multi-stage Pipeline with Inter-core On-chip Sharing
methods.name_zh: 多阶段流水＋跨核片上共享
methods.summary: Exchange producer-consumer tiles through a verified inter-core on-chip sharing mechanism.
graph_conditions: Stages can exchange ready tiles within a supported sharing scope.
Separate resource roles expose useful pipeline work.
case_features: Intermediate traffic matters but one local region is inefficient.
Stages benefit from separate resource assignments.
hardware_requirements: Verified shared-memory addressing, scope, lifetime and visibility.
Backend/runtime support; separate launches may not preserve on-chip state.
Valid synchronization and forward-progress guarantees.
methods.execution_organization: Partition roles within a supported cooperative scope; use separate kernels only with explicit shared-state support.
methods.dataflow: Producer tile -> verified shared on-chip storage -> ordered consumer access -> output; L2 caching alone is insufficient.
benefits: Separate schedules with a larger shared on-chip working set.
risks: Required platform primitives may be absent.
Contention, lifetime errors, synchronization or deadlock.
Mistaking likely cache reuse for guaranteed sharing.

variants.name: Cooperative shared-tile stages
variants.description: Exchange tiles across execution units within a verified sharing and scheduling scope.

variants.name: Explicitly supported cross-kernel sharing
variants.description: Use separate kernels only with proven persistent sharing and ordering support; otherwise reject.

implementation_checks: Identify actual memory, API and synchronization support.
Verify scope, capacity, lifetime, ordering and progress.
Measure traffic/stalls; cache capacity is not evidence of HBM elimination.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.
source_sections: F6: Multi-stage Pipeline with Inter-core On-chip Sharing（跨核片上共享流水）

methods.name: Split and Fusion Co-optimization
methods.summary: Jointly search legal decompositions and fusion partitions using reuse, resource and measurement evidence.
graph_conditions: Compound operations admit equivalent primitive decompositions.
Several legal boundaries create a meaningful search space.
case_features: Long/branching graphs have competing locality and resource needs.
Fixed all-fused or all-split policies miss bottlenecks.
hardware_requirements: Backend can express candidate groups.
Resource constraints and a cost model or measurement budget.
methods.execution_organization: Analyze reuse/dependencies, propose legal partitions, then compare concrete kernel groupings.
methods.dataflow: Retain data within selected groups; materialize or explicitly communicate across their boundaries.
benefits: Find better boundaries than the initial plan.
risks: Search/compilation cost and model error.
Invalid decomposition or numerical changes.

variants.name: Reuse-guided partition search
variants.description: Use locality and graph dependencies to propose split points and fusion groups.

variants.name: Cost-guided legal grouping
variants.description: Search legal groupings with a suitable cost model or graph-based procedure, then measure candidates.

implementation_checks: Prove decomposition equivalence and precision.
Bound search and retain a correct incumbent.
Measure promising plans on all required cases.
Record the concrete plan, not just the search algorithm.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.
source_sections: F7: Split and Fusion Co-optimization（拆分融合协同搜索）

methods.name: Joint Compute-Memory Fusion
methods.summary: Jointly schedule compute-heavy stages and memory-heavy subgraphs to reduce materialization or overlap work.
graph_conditions: Compute connects to elementwise, reduction or layout subgraphs.
Tile dependencies allow a staged schedule.
case_features: Alternating compute/memory stages leave traffic or idle resources.
Back-to-back compute has a transformable intervening subgraph.
hardware_requirements: Backend supports the proposed staged operations/schedule.
Supported overlap, buffers and dependency synchronization.
methods.execution_organization: Assign compute and memory work to supported stages/streams; compiler scheduling still enforces dependencies.
methods.dataflow: Ready tiles feed memory and later compute stages through valid buffers; distinguish removed from merely overlapped materialization.
benefits: Jointly optimize layout, reuse and overlap.
risks: Unsupported schedule or hidden materialization.
Buffering, contention and synchronization exceed gains.
Serial dependencies limit concurrency.

variants.name: Compute / memory-subgraph pipeline
variants.description: Pipeline compute tiles with connected elementwise, layout or reduction work and valid dependencies.

variants.name: Back-to-back compute stages
variants.description: Jointly schedule consecutive compute stages and transforms when layouts/reductions permit.

implementation_checks: Inspect generated execution and traffic, not stream names.
Verify buffer lifetime and all dependencies.
Compare utilization and complete-scope latency with F1/F2.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.
source_sections: F8: Joint Compute-Memory Fusion（计算访存联合融合）

methods.name: Deep Kernel Fusion
methods.summary: Fuse a longer multi-operation region when a legal tiled schedule efficiently retains its live state.
graph_conditions: A region contains multiple dependent compute/transform stages.
Dependencies, reductions and outputs admit one kernel schedule.
case_features: Long chains or MLP-like graphs repeatedly materialize activations.
Ordinary two-operation chains generally fit F2.
hardware_requirements: Backend supports the entire selected region.
Enough live tiled-state capacity and valid synchronization.
methods.execution_organization: One kernel schedules multiple stages, with tiling, pipelining or justified recomputation to bound live state.
methods.dataflow: Input -> locally retained live tiles across stages -> outputs; full tensors need not all reside on chip together.
benefits: Remove traffic and launches across a larger region.
risks: Spills, reduced occupancy and complex reductions.
Coordination or recomputation exceeds traffic savings.
Deeper fusion can be slower.

variants.name: Deep dependent chain
variants.description: Fuse a multi-stage compute/activation chain with explicit live-state analysis.

variants.name: Deep region with shared branches
variants.description: Fuse a larger shared-branch region with legal output scheduling; combine F4 where applicable.

implementation_checks: Analyze dependencies and live state stage by stage.
Inspect spills, recomputation, reduction precision and synchronization.
Compare sensible partial-fusion plans on all cases.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.
source_sections: F9: Deep Kernel Fusion（长链深度融合）

methods.name: Multi-device Compute-Communication Fusion
methods.summary: Jointly schedule distributed compute and communication with supported tile-level overlap.
graph_conditions: The contract includes communication across devices/nodes.
Tiles have well-defined distributed readiness and ordering.
case_features: Communication materially affects distributed latency.
Single-device compute-only tasks give no direct reason to select F10.
hardware_requirements: Relevant topology and communication primitives.
Supported device-side progress or another valid overlap mechanism.
Cross-device ordering and visibility guarantees.
methods.execution_organization: Assign compute/communication roles in a supported distributed model; persistent execution is optional and capability-dependent.
methods.dataflow: Local tiles <-> supported transport <-> remote compute -> distributed outputs with valid communication semantics.
benefits: Potentially reduce launches or global stage barriers.
risks: Missing device-side support, topology limits and contention.
Deadlock, progress failure or collective-order errors.
Hidden transfer/preprocessing costs.

variants.name: Intra-node compute / communication pipeline
variants.description: Overlap intra-node transport and compute using the actual supported communication API.

variants.name: Inter-node compute / communication pipeline
variants.description: Pipeline across nodes only with verified transport, progress and synchronization support.

implementation_checks: Confirm task communication and participating devices.
Validate distributed correctness, ordering and progress.
Benchmark the full workload with consistent topology and scope.
Verify the required Triton Ascend operations and compiler options on the installed backend; preserve the task interface, strides, masks, dtype and measured work scope.
